bluf: LocaliQ is a US, AI powered marketing platform with local experts, selling search, display, video and social ads, email, listings, websites, SEO and Dash AI lead management to local and multi location businesses, claiming 512K+ businesses served. It is doing product launches at pace: Dash Scheduler in 2026-03, a full AI agents suite in 2026-06, Demand Builder in 2026-08, G2 Fall 2026 category wins in 2026-09. Where it is going: agents that run the SMB's lead handling, not just its ads. The thing a rival should know: the Monsoon displacement read of 72.3 says its book buys on price, and it shows no AI assistant ad test.
doing:
LocaliQ positions itself as an end to end, AI powered marketing platform with local experts helping local and multi location businesses find leads, get found and convert. In plain words: a scaled SMB marketing vendor that sells media, listings, websites and lead software as one package, with humans attached. Its headline claim is that 512K+ businesses trust it and that optimization draws on data from 5.9M campaigns, quoted as its claims.

The sold mix leads with AI automation (scored 3: the title reads AI powered, Dash AI lead management, a June 2026 AI agents suite) and local (scored 3: the meta pitches marketing for local businesses, a listings product, a multi location offer, local expert support). Three lines score 2 and sit in the core: email and CRM (a lead conversion page with AI lead management, automated email and CRM linked ROAS reporting, a Dash case study), paid search (Google Ads graders and an AI copy tool leading the nav, a search ads product, a Microsoft Ads ROAS case) and programmatic and CTV (display ads, video ads, cross media optimization and USA TODAY Network placements in the nav). Proprietary: Dash by LocaliQ, Dash Scheduler, the AI agents suite, Demand Builder, two Google Ads graders and a Website Grader. No partners are listed.

AI posture: Dash categorizes, summarizes and prioritizes leads, a 2026 AI agent suite, and generative AI SEO and Google Ads AI copy tools. Moves in date order: 2026-03, Dash Scheduler and ROAS reporting with CRM integration; 2026-06, a full suite of AI agents for always on business; 2026-08, Demand Builder, to reach customers before they start searching; 2026-08, the AI Innovation Award in the 2026 MarTech Breakthrough Awards; 2026-09, top rankings in G2's Fall 2026 report. Pricing signals: none, the conspicuous absence for an SMB platform of its kind, alongside no LSA or Sponsored Places work despite selling local at depth, and no B2B, CRO or content line.
clients:
The record types the client as local: local and multi location businesses across home services, healthcare, automotive, professional services, legal, education, travel and entertainment, retail, finance, real estate and multi location. The home market is the US, with Australia and New Zealand listed as offices and case study pages for Brisbane, Auckland, Queensland, Canberra and Sydney.

The needs read lists 12 clients, 4 observed and 8 named only, from 9 case studies and 3 slugs. Procelsio Clinic came for local and lead generation, its case titled Reaches New Markets and Leads with LocaliQ; B&W Plumbing came for the same, its case titled on securing long term business growth; SOBRsafe came for B2B pipeline, its case saying LocaliQ powers its B2C and B2B revenue streams; Mr. Handyman (Huntsville) came for local and lead generation, its case titled on revenue and leads. The observed mix is local and lead generation and B2B pipeline. The other 8 are names only: Cowley College, Travel Insurance Office, Mission Golf Cars, Maggs McDermott & DiCicco, Lukas Nursery, Dean McGee Eye Institute, Crazy Clark's Car Rentals and Rova Rentals, with needs inferred from what the platform leads with. The Australia and New Zealand case pages are by trade (college education, health training, personal injury lawyers, accountants, mortgage brokers) rather than by name. No client is shared with another tracked agency.

What the base needs next: the Horus read places LocaliQ best for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) and KJ2 (ads inside AI answers), driven by AI search and paid search, and most exposed to KJ5 (the price of attention splits in two) and KJ7 (local discovery is being enclosed). It is likely, with moderate confidence, that this SMB book will need presence inside enclosed local discovery (LSAs, Sponsored Places) and assistant answers, neither of which the record shows LocaliQ selling.
house:
Say and do: 1 of 1 tested lines is practised on its own house. Paid search is corroborated: it runs its own Google ads, 21 in the Transparency Center and 14 in the last 30 days, 17 text, 3 image and 1 video, under LocaliQ and its sister brand WordStream, Inc., last shown 2026-09-27; a sample reads Reach the right customers at the right time with AI powered marketing. LinkedIn: 7 company page ads and 0 thought leader ads, with 6 thought leader ads paid for by Wordstream not counted; a sample reads Scale your digital marketing with LocaliQ, AI powered optimization, dedicated partner support, and bigger ROI. No gaps were flagged.

Content velocity is high: the sitemap lists 1765 URLs, 144 updated in 90 days and 396 in 365, it publishes llms.txt, blocks no AI crawlers and carries 5 AI URLs. The site is WordPress with GTM and OneTrust only: no social pixels, testing tools or ABM stack detected.
market:
The Horus read scores LocaliQ at a tailwind index of 11.6, band Favored, say and do integrity 100. Best placed for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) and KJ2 (ads inside AI answers), both driven by AI search and paid search. Most exposed to KJ5 (the price of attention splits in two) and KJ7 (local discovery is being enclosed, local at -1). Best fit: The Walled Oasis at 36/100. Moves: making P7 (owned audiences and steady publishing), partial on P1 (AI visibility sold, not audited), P3 (no LSA or Sponsored Places work), P4 and P6, unknown on P5, absent on P2 and P8.

The Monsoon read: index 62.3, band Onshore wind, 76th percentile; migration 52.3 against displacement 72.3, a local ICP term of 12 and a scaled segment term of 8 pushing it up. The verdict puts 52 of the index on the sold mix, local (14) and paid search (7), and sends the work 65% to South and Southeast Asia and 25% to Latin America, all inferred: no hub office or onshore claim is listed.
openings:
The strongest opening is price against a book that buys on it. The Monsoon displacement read of 72.3 (inferred) sits well above its migration read of 52.3, and LocaliQ publishes no pricing model. It is likely, with moderate confidence, that an offshore delivered rival with a transparent, outcome priced SMB offer can undercut it line by line on local, paid search and email. Falsifier: LocaliQ publishing plan pricing tied to leads or bookings.

Second, the enclosed local layer: it sells local at depth with no LSA or Sponsored Places work in the record (P3 partial) and no feed, schema or entity line (P2 absent), so the places where KJ7 says local discovery is being enclosed are unclaimed by the vendor of listings. Third, no sign of testing ads inside AI assistants on a paid search line (P8 absent): the first SMB platform to show assistant ad results sets the price. Fourth, its paid media runs without first party data or measurement depth showing (P4 partial). Fifth, 8 of 12 clients are names only, though the AI lead handling in Dash is a real product a rival must match rather than talk past.
watch: I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the next milestone ($2B) and its timing, and pricing below $20 CPM, would open the assistant ad channel it has not tested and feed KJ2, its second tailwind.

I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, next reading late October 2026: search and other growth below 10% flags cannibalization of the paid search line, while above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and KJ1.
I4, Meta Q3 2026 average price per ad, next reading late October 2026: at or above +5% continues walled garden inflation and deepens KJ5, its largest exposure, on the social and display lines.
I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, next reading late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk behind KJ1.
The dated moves to follow are Demand Builder (2026-08) and the AI agents suite (2026-06): a case study with numbers for either would turn the AI automation lead from a launch cadence into proof.
